newsitem.title: FRANCE: French bourse's CAC index sets record close.
newsitem.headline: French bourse's CAC index sets record close.

text.p: The French stockmarket's CAC-40 index set a closing record of 2,361.27 points on Monday, surpassing the previous closing record of 2,355.93 set on February 2, 1994, the French stockmarkets association SBF said.
The French blue chip index also set a new intraday high of 2,371.38 points, up from the previous high of 2,360.98.
It rose 1.4 percent on Monday in a rally fuelled by Wall Street's rise to a fresh record on Friday and bolstered by expectations of higher corporate earnings this year.

"The fundamentals are good for the bourse, and they haven't changed -- interest rates are low, corporate profits are expected to rise on moderate economic growth, productivity is improving, and exchange rates are favourable with the franc's decline against the Italian lira, British sterling and dollar," said George de Nesmeskery Kiss, economist at Societe Generale.

Brokers were divided over the French market's near-term outlook, with some predicting a correction. But most said they expected it to rise to around 2,450 points in the medium to long term. The market's immediate focus will be on the U.S. consumer inflation figures due for release on Tuesday at 1330 GMT.
* Carmaker Renault's stock, which has languished near all-time lows for weeks, showed the biggest gain in the CAC index. It rose 4.15 percent to 113 francs.
Chairman Louis Schweitzer said in an interview with the Figaro that the car operation's losses deepened in 1996 but that he hoped for a break-even this year in the division.
The stock has also been helped by reports describing the huge popularity of the new Megane Scenic model.
* Rival PSA Peugeot Citroen closed down 0.37 percent at 542 francs after J.P. Morgan cut its profit forecast for the group for 1997, saying it saw no let-up in a price war.
* Shares in oil majors Elf Aquitaine and Total rose on gains in crude prices and in the dollar.

Brokers said Elf, which closed up 1.6 percent at 495.70 francs, was helped by an oil exploration deal signed with the government of Azerbaijan. They said Total, which finished up 1.51 percent at 424.30 francs, was helped by PaineWebber's initiation of coverage of the stock.

* Shares in pharmaceuticals firm Sanofi finished down 2.64 percent at 553 francs, giving up around half of their gains on Friday on merger talk, after the company denied rumours that it was linking up with Synthelabo.
* The dollar's gains also boosted shares in tyremaker Michelin, which rose 2.59 percent to 289.50 francs.
* LVMH rose 1.56 percent to 1,430 francs. It said on Saturday that it had closed the DFS acquisition.
* Air Liquide rose 2.68 percent to 843 francs after brokerage Gilbert Dupont raised its rating on the stock.

* Brokers say cyclical shares may feature more actively in the market's continued advance. They expect interest to run high in the restructuring pharmaceuticals and retail sectors and selective buying in the long-suffering financial sector.
* Volume on Monday was a very heavy 7.7 billion francs.
